description: Bare bulb under a shallow pressed enamel dish shade, hung over a market stall on its own flex

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Hanging light fitting made of a shallow pressed metal dish shade, a wide smooth cone flaring down and out from a small domed crown at the top, a short thick stem standing up from the crown ending in a small ring to hang it by, and hanging under the shade a stout lamp holder cylinder with a single large pear-shaped bulb screwed into it, the bulb hanging clear below the rim of the shade Materials: Chipped white vitreous enamel over steel with a black rolled rim, rust blooming through every chip and around the crown, soot and cooking grease filming the inside of the shade, dust on the outer face, a clear glass bulb clouded and greasy with a dark filament and a brass base gone green.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.33 x 0.534 x 0.33 m. Cost: 1360 triangles / 4000, 2 draw calls / 4, 2 materials / 3, 2 unique geometries / 6, 1 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.999, 0.988, 1.008], interior hole fractions [0.0068, 0.012, 0.011, 0.0063]).  Two components at 2 draw calls, 2 materials and 2 geometries against a large ceiling of 4/3/6 -- half the draw-call budget, which matters because the asset notes place these in rows of a dozen over one market aisle.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.330 x 0.534 x 0.330 m against the declared 0.32 x 0.55 x 0.32 -- 3% over on width and depth (the navy rim ring standing proud of the dish's r 0.16) and 3% under on height. The dish was flattened during the rebuild: at a 0.20 m rim it was a steep cone where the plate reads depth/width about 0.33, and the holder was lengthened to carry the fixture to its declared hang.

A shallow straight-sided dish built as a SHELL -- down the outside, across the rim's thickness and back up the inside -- with its inner face tinted a shade darker so the opening reads as an opening. A single-sided cone would show backfaces from below, and the previous build was a closed bell curve. The dark navy rim band is a separate ring standing 2-5 mm proud of the edge so the two never share a surface; the previous build had no rim at all, and it is the strongest line on the fixture.

A brass holder barrel and skirt between the dish and a teardrop bulb widest BELOW its middle with a real neck. The previous build ran a smooth blob straight into the shade with no holder. The gate runs with --allow-holes: at azimuths 90 and 180 the enclosed region is a sparse 50 x 61 px area at 32% fill under the dish and beside the bulb neck, which is the air an OPEN dish shade genuinely has under it -- verified by sampling rather than assumed.

Two material layers: vitreous enamel at roughness 0.34 -- glossy, which is what separates it from the matt cloth lanterns elsewhere in this kit -- carrying its darker inner face and navy rim as vertex colours plus a chipped-enamel tile, and one brass-and-glass material for the holder and bulb. The NAVY is authored at luma 31 rather than the ~42 it measures: the harness renders about 1.29x brighter than albedo, so 42 would come back near 54, close enough to gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window that the rim's curvature would sweep pixels into it.

name: Enamel Shade Market Bulb
nameTh: โคมไฟกะลาแขวน
notes:
The bare bulb under a pressed enamel dish that lights every fresh market and night stall -- hung on its own flex from a canopy frame, and placed in rows of a dozen. The shade is about 0.3 m across and the whole fixture hangs 0.55 m; the height figure is the shade, holder and bulb, not the flex, because the flex length belongs to whatever it hangs from. Pivot is top-center so it hangs from the ring. It is distinct from the twin-tube fluorescent batten already in the kit, which is a rigid ceiling-mounted fitting rather than a hanging one. Static: hung, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
